note.question: How do externalities affect cooperative approaches to managing social responsibility in a market?
note.overview: This paper studies two cooperative approaches of firms in managing social responsibility violations of their supplier: auditing a common supplier jointly (joint auditing) and sharing independent audit results with other firms (audit sharing). This paper studies this problem in a market with externalities and a large number of firms. With numerous firms procuring their materials and parts worldwide, there are many cases in which overseas suppliers violate safety, labor, or environmental standards.

One can see from (13) that the positive externality (determined by γ) does not affect the profit, because manufacturers have the same social responsibility level after the supplier’s problem is corrected.
